ABDOMEN: The region of the body of a vertebrate between the thorax and the pelvis.
ADENOID: A collection of lymphatic tissue in the throat behind the uvula.
ADRENAL: Either of a pair of complex endocrine glands situated near the kidney.
ADRENALINE: A catecholamine secreted by the adrenal medulla in response to stress.
ALLERGEN: Any substance that can cause an allergy.
ALVEOLI: A tiny sac for holding air in the lungs; formed by the terminal dilation of tiny air passageways.
ALVEOLUS: A tiny sac for holding air in the lungs; formed by the terminal dilation of tiny air passageways.
ANAEMIA: A lack of red blood cells or haemoglobin in the blood.
ANEMIA: A lack of red blood cells or haemoglobin in the blood.
ANKLE: A gliding joint between the distal ends of the tibia and fibula and the proximal end of the talus.
ANTIBODY: A protein made by the immune system that recognises and neutralises germs.
ANTIGEN: Any substance that stimulates an immune response in the body.
AORTA: The large trunk artery that carries blood from the left ventricle of the heart to branch arteries.
AORTIC: Of or relating to the aorta.
APPENDIX: A vestigial process that extends from the lower end of the cecum and that resembles a small pouch.
ARMPIT: The hollow under the arm where it is joined to the shoulder.
ARTERIOLE: One of the small thin-walled arteries that end in capillaries.
ARTERY: A blood vessel that carries blood from the heart to the body.
ARTHRITIS: Inflammation of a joint or joints.
ATRIUM: Either of the two upper chambers of the heart.
AXON: Long nerve fiber that conducts away from the cell body of the neuron.
BACK: The posterior part of a human body from the neck to the end of the spine.
BACKBONE: The series of vertebrae forming the axis of the skeleton and protecting the spinal cord.
BACTERIUM: A single-celled microorganism; some cause disease and others aid digestion.
BICEP: The large muscle at the front of the upper arm.
BICEPS: The large muscle at the front of the upper arm.
BLADDER: The sac that stores urine before it leaves the body.
BLOOD: The fluid that is pumped through the body by the heart and contains plasma, blood cells.
BONE: Rigid connective tissue that makes up the skeleton of vertebrates.
BOWEL: The part of the alimentary canal between the stomach and the anus.
BRAIN: That part of the central nervous system that includes all the higher nervous centers.
BRAINSTEM: The part of the brain continuous with the spinal cord and comprising the medulla oblongata.
BREAST: The front of the trunk from the neck to the abdomen.
BRONCHI: Either of the two main branches of the trachea.
BRONCHIOLE: Any of the smallest bronchial ducts; ending in alveoli.
BUTTOCK: Either of the two large fleshy masses of muscular tissue that form the human rump.
CALCIUM: A mineral, the main element in bones and teeth.
CALF: The fleshy back part of the leg below the knee.
CAPILLARY: Any of the minute blood vessels connecting arterioles with venules.
CAPSULE: A structure that encloses a body part.
CARDIAC: Of or relating to the heart.
CARTILAGE: Tough elastic tissue; mostly converted to bone in adults.
CEREBELLUM: A major division of the vertebrate brain; situated above the medulla oblongata.
CEREBRAL: Of or relating to the cerebrum or brain.
CEREBRUM: Anterior portion of the brain consisting of two hemispheres; dominant part of the brain in humans.
CERVIX: The narrow lower end of the uterus.
CHEEK: Either side of the face below the eyes.
CHEST: The part of the human torso between the neck and the diaphragm or the corresponding part.
CHIN: The protruding part of the lower jaw.
CHOLESTEROL: An animal sterol that is normally synthesized by the liver.
CHROMATIN: The readily stainable substance of a cell nucleus consisting of DNA and RNA and various proteins.
CHROMOSOME: A threadlike strand of DNA in the cell nucleus that carries the genes in a linear order.
CILIA: Tiny hair-like projections on the surface of some cells, such as those lining the airways.
CLAVICLE: Bone linking the scapula and sternum.
COCCYX: The end of the vertebral column in humans and tailless apes.
COLLAGEN: A fibrous scleroprotein in bone and cartilage and tendon and other connective tissue.
COLLARBONE: Bone linking the scapula and sternum.
COLON: The part of the large intestine between the cecum and the rectum.
CONCUSSION: Injury to the brain caused by a blow; usually resulting in loss of consciousness.
CORNEA: The transparent dome-shaped anterior portion of the outer covering of the eye.
CORPUSCLE: A blood cell, red or white.
CORTEX: The outer layer of an organ, especially the folded grey matter of the brain.
CRANIUM: The part of the skull that encloses the brain.
CUTICLE: The dead skin at the base of a fingernail or toenail.
CYTOPLASM: The protoplasm of a cell excluding the nucleus; is full of proteins that control cell metabolism.
DEHYDRATION: Dryness resulting from the removal of water.
DELTOID: The large triangular muscle covering the shoulder joint.
DENDRITE: Short fiber that conducts toward the cell body of the neuron.
DERMIS: The deep vascular inner layer of the skin.
DIAPHRAGM: A muscular partition separating the abdominal and thoracic cavities; functions in respiration.
DIASTOLE: The widening of the chambers of the heart between two contractions when the chambers fill with blood.
DIGESTIVE: Relating to or having the power to cause or promote digestion.
DIGIT: A finger or toe in human beings or corresponding body part in other vertebrates.
DILATION: Widening or enlarging, as of the pupils or blood vessels.
DIMPLE: A small natural hollow in the cheek or chin.
DISC: A pad of cartilage between two vertebrae of the spine.
DUODENUM: The part of the small intestine between the stomach and the jejunum.
EARDRUM: The membrane in the ear that vibrates to sound.
EARLOBE: The fleshy pendulous part of the external human ear.
ELBOW: Hinge joint between the forearm and upper arm and the corresponding joint.
ENAMEL: Hard white substance covering the crown of a tooth.
ENDOCRINE: Of glands: releasing hormones directly into the blood.
ENDORPHIN: A neurochemical occurring naturally in the brain and having analgesic properties.
ENZYME: A protein made by cells that speeds up chemical reactions in the body.
EPIDERMIS: The outer layer of the skin covering the exterior body surface of vertebrates.
EPIGLOTTIS: A flap of cartilage that covers the windpipe while swallowing.
ESOPHAGUS: The passage between the pharynx and the stomach.
EYEBALL: The ball-shaped capsule containing the vertebrate eye.
EYEBROW: The arch of hair above each eye.
EYELASH: Any of the short curved hairs that grow from the edges of the eyelids.
EYELID: Either of two folds of skin that can be moved to cover or open the eye.
FACE: The front of the human head from the forehead to the chin and ear to ear.
FASCIA: A sheet or band of fibrous connective tissue separating or binding together muscles and organs etc.
FATIGUE: Temporary loss of strength and energy resulting from hard physical or mental work.
FEMORAL: Of or relating to or near the femur or thigh.
FEMUR: The longest and thickest bone of the human skeleton; extends from the pelvis to the knee.
FIBROSIS: Development of excess fibrous connective tissue in an organ.
FIBULA: The outer and thinner of the two bones of the human leg between the knee and ankle.
FINGER: Any of the terminal members of the hand.
FINGERNAIL: The nail at the end of a finger.
FIST: A hand with the fingers clenched in the palm.
FOLLICLE: Any small spherical group of cells containing a cavity.
FONTANEL: Any membranous gap between the bones of the cranium in an infant or fetus.
FONTANELLE: Any membranous gap between the bones of the cranium in an infant or fetus.
FOOT: The part of the leg of a human being below the ankle joint.
FOREARM: The part of the superior limb between the elbow and the wrist.
FOREHEAD: The part of the face above the eyes.
FRECKLE: A small brownish spot on the skin.
GALLBLADDER: A muscular sac attached to the liver that stores bile until it is needed for digestion.
GALLSTONE: A small hard mass that forms in the gallbladder.
GANGLION: An encapsulated neural structure consisting of a collection of cell bodies or neurons.
GASTRIC: Relating to or involving the stomach.
GENETIC: Of or relating to or produced by or being a gene.
GENOME: The complete set of genes or genetic material in a cell or organism.
GLAND: An organ that makes and releases substances such as hormones, sweat or saliva.
GLUCOSE: A monosaccharide sugar that has several forms; an important source of physiological energy.
GLUTEUS: Any one of three large skeletal muscles that form the buttock and move the thigh.
GLYCOGEN: The form in which the body stores glucose, mainly in the liver and muscles.
GROIN: The fold where the inner thigh meets the lower abdomen.
HAEMATOMA: A localized swelling filled with blood.
HAEMOGLOBIN: A hemoprotein composed of globin and heme that gives red blood cells their characteristic color.
HAEMORRHAGE: The flow of blood from a ruptured blood vessel.
HAIR: A covering for the body consisting of a dense growth of threadlike structures.
HAMSTRING: One of the tendons or muscles at the back of the thigh and knee.
HAND: The part of the arm below the wrist, with the palm, fingers and thumb.
HEAD: The upper part of the human body or the front part of the body in animals.
HEART: The hollow muscular organ located behind the sternum and between the lungs.
HEARTBEAT: One full contraction and relaxation of the heart.
HEEL: The back part of the human foot.
HEMATOMA: A localized swelling filled with blood.
HEMOGLOBIN: A hemoprotein composed of globin and heme that gives red blood cells their characteristic color.
HEMORRHAGE: The flow of blood from a ruptured blood vessel.
HORMONAL: Of or relating to or caused by hormones.
HORMONE: A chemical messenger made by a gland and carried in the blood to act elsewhere.
HYDRATION: Taking in enough water to keep the body working properly.
IMMUNE: Relating to the condition of immunity.
IMMUNITY: The body's ability to resist an infection or disease.
INCISOR: A tooth for cutting or gnawing; located in the front of the mouth in both jaws.
INFECTION: The pathological state resulting from the invasion of the body by pathogenic microorganisms.
INSULIN: Hormone secreted by the isles of Langerhans in the pancreas.
INTESTINE: The part of the alimentary canal between the stomach and the anus.
IRIS: Muscular diaphragm that controls the size of the pupil.
ISCHIUM: One of the three sections of the hipbone; situated below the ilium.
JAWLINE: The outline of the lower jaw.
JEJUNUM: The part of the small intestine between the duodenum and the ileum.
JOINT: The point of connection between two bones or elements of a skeleton.
KERATIN: The tough protein that makes up hair, nails and the outer layer of skin.
KERATOSIS: A skin condition marked by an overgrowth of layers of horny skin.
KIDNEY: Either of two bean-shaped excretory organs that filter wastes.
KNEE: The joint between the thigh and the lower leg.
KNEECAP: A small flat triangular bone in front of the knee that protects the knee joint.
KNUCKLE: A joint of a finger when the fist is closed.
LACTATE: A salt or ester of lactic acid.
LARYNGEAL: Of or relating to or situated in the larynx.
LARYNX: A cartilaginous structure at the top of the trachea.
LATISSIMUS: The broad, flat muscle of the lower back that pulls the arms down and back.
LESION: Any localized abnormal structural change in a bodily part.
LEUKAEMIA: Malignant neoplasm of blood-forming tissues; characterized by abnormal proliferation of leukocytes.
LEUKEMIA: Malignant neoplasm of blood-forming tissues; characterized by abnormal proliferation of leukocytes.
LEUKOCYTE: Blood cells that engulf and digest bacteria and fungi.
LIGAMENT: A sheet or band of tough fibrous tissue connecting bones or cartilages or supporting muscles.
LIMB: One of the jointed appendages of an animal used for locomotion or grasping: arm; leg; wing; flipper.
LIPID: An oily organic compound insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents.
LIVER: A large reddish-brown organ that cleans the blood, stores nutrients and makes bile.
LOBE: A somewhat rounded subdivision of a bodily organ or part.
LUMBAR: Of or relating to or near the part of the back between the ribs and the hipbones.
LUNG: Either of two saclike respiratory organs in the chest of vertebrates.
LYMPH: A thin coagulable fluid containing white blood cells and chyle.
LYMPHATIC: Of or relating to or produced by lymph.
MANDIBLE: The jaw in vertebrates that is hinged to open the mouth.
MARROW: The fatty network of connective tissue that fills the cavities of bones.
MEDULLA: Lower or hindmost part of the brain; continuous with spinal cord.
MELANIN: Insoluble pigments that account for the color of e.g. skin and scales and feathers.
MELATONIN: Hormone secreted by the pineal gland.
MEMBRANE: A pliable sheet of tissue that covers or lines or connects the organs or cells of animals or plants.
METABOLISM: The chemical processes by which the body turns food into energy and builds tissue.
MIGRAINE: A severe recurring vascular headache; occurs more frequently in women than men.
MITOCHONDRIA: An organelle containing enzymes responsible for producing energy.
MOLAR: Grinding tooth with a broad crown; located behind the premolars.
MOLE: A small dark raised spot on the skin.
MOLECULE: The simplest structural unit of an element or compound.
MOTOR: Of nerves or muscles: producing movement.
MOUTH: The opening through which food is taken in and vocalizations emerge.
MUCOSA: Mucus-secreting membrane lining all body cavities or passages that communicate with the exterior.
MUCOUS: Of or secreting or covered with or resembling mucus.
MUCUS: Protective secretion of the mucus membranes; in the gut it lubricates the passage.
MUSCLE: One of the contractile organs of the body.
MUSCULAR: Of or relating to or consisting of muscle.
MYOCARDIUM: The middle muscular layer of the heart wall.
NAIL: Horny plate covering and protecting part of the dorsal surface of the digits.
NAPE: The back side of the neck.
NASAL: Of or relating to the nose.
NAVEL: A scar where the umbilical cord was attached.
NECK: The part of an organism that connects the head to the rest of the body.
NERVE: Any bundle of nerve fibers running to various organs and tissues of the body.
NEURAL: Of or relating to the nervous system.
NEURON: A cell that is specialized to conduct nerve impulses.
NIPPLE: The small projection of a mammary gland.
NOSE: The organ of smell and entrance to the respiratory tract.
NOSTRIL: Either one of the two external openings to the nasal cavity in the nose.
NUCLEIC: Of acids such as DNA and RNA, found in cell nuclei.
NUCLEUS: A part of the cell containing DNA and RNA and responsible for growth and reproduction.
NUTRIENT: A substance in food that the body needs to live and grow.
OBLIQUES: A diagonally arranged abdominal muscle on either side of the torso.
OESOPHAGUS: The passage between the pharynx and the stomach.
OPTIC: Of or relating to the eye or sight.
ORGAN: A fully differentiated structural and functional unit in an animal.
ORGANISM: A living thing, such as an animal, plant or microbe.
OSSICLE: A small bone; especially one in the middle ear.
OVARY: One of usually two organs that produce ova and secrete estrogen and progesterone.
OXYGEN: The gas the body takes in by breathing, needed by every cell.
OXYGENATED: Of blood: carrying oxygen from the lungs.
PALATE: The upper surface of the mouth that separates the oral and nasal cavities.
PALM: The inner surface of the hand from the wrist to the base of the fingers.
PANCREAS: A large elongated exocrine gland located behind the stomach; secretes pancreatic juice and insulin.
PAROTID: Relating to or located near the parotid gland.
PATELLA: A small flat triangular bone in front of the knee that protects the knee joint.
PATHOGEN: A germ, such as a bacterium or virus, that causes disease.
PECTORAL: Either of two large muscles of the chest.
PELVIC: Of or relating to the pelvis.
PELVIS: The structure of the vertebrate skeleton supporting the lower limbs.
PEPTIDE: Amide combining the amino group of one amino acid with the carboxyl group of another.
PERIOSTEUM: The tough membrane covering the surface of bones.
PERIPHERAL: Of nerves or vessels: lying away from the centre of the body.
PHALANX: Any of the bones of the fingers or toes.
PHARYNX: The cavity behind the nose and mouth that leads to the oesophagus and windpipe.
PHLEGM: Expectorated matter; saliva mixed with discharges from the respiratory passages.
PIGMENT: A substance, such as melanin, that gives skin, hair or eyes their colour.
PINKY: The finger farthest from the thumb.
PITUITARY: The master gland of the endocrine system; located at the base of the brain.
PLASMA: The colorless watery fluid of the blood and lymph that contains no cells.
PLATELET: Tiny bits of protoplasm found in vertebrate blood; essential for blood clotting.
PORE: Any small opening in the skin or outer surface of an animal.
PORTAL: A short vein that carries blood into the liver.
POSTURE: The way the body is held when standing or sitting.
PROTEIN: A large molecule made of amino acids, a building block of muscle and other tissue.
PULMONARY: Relating to or affecting the lungs.
PULMONIC: Relating to or affecting the lungs.
PULSE: The regular throb of the arteries as the heart pumps blood.
PUPIL: The contractile aperture in the center of the iris of the eye; resembles a large black dot.
QUADRICEPS: A muscle of the thigh that extends the leg.
RECEPTOR: A structure on a cell that responds to a particular chemical or stimulus.
REFLEX: An automatic movement made in response to a stimulus, such as a knee jerk.
RENAL: Of or relating to the kidneys.
RESPIRATION: Breathing; also the process by which cells release energy from food.
RETINA: The innermost light-sensitive membrane covering the back wall of the eyeball.
RETINAL: In or relating to the retina of the eye.
RIBCAGE: The bony enclosing wall of the chest.
RIBOSOME: An organelle in the cytoplasm of a living cell; they attach to mRNA.
SACRUM: Wedge-shaped bone consisting of five fused vertebrae forming the posterior part of the pelvis.
SALIVA: A clear liquid secreted into the mouth by the salivary glands and mucous glands of the mouth.
SCALP: The skin that covers the top of the head.
SCAPULA: Either of two flat triangular bones one on each side of the shoulder in human beings.
SCAR: A mark left by the healing of injured tissue.
SCIATIC: Of or relating to the hip, or the sciatic nerve running down the leg.
SCLERA: The whitish fibrous membrane that with the cornea forms the outer covering and protection.
SECRETION: A functionally specialized substance released from a gland or cell.
SEIZURE: A sudden burst of abnormal brain activity, causing convulsions or loss of awareness.
SEPTUM: A dividing partition between two tissues or cavities.
SEROTONIN: A neurotransmitter involved in e.g. sleep and depression and memory.
SHIN: The front part of the human leg between the knee and the ankle.
SHOULDER: The part of the body between the neck and the upper arm.
SINEW: A cord or band of inelastic tissue connecting a muscle with its bony attachment.
SINUS: One of the air-filled cavities in the skull bones around the nose.
SKELETAL: Of or relating to or forming or attached to a skeleton.
SKELETON: The hard structure that provides a frame for the body of an animal.
SKIN: A natural protective body covering and site of the sense of touch.
SKULL: The bony skeleton of the head of vertebrates.
SPASM: A painful and involuntary muscular contraction.
SPINAL: Of or relating to the spine or spinal cord.
SPINE: The series of vertebrae forming the axis of the skeleton and protecting the spinal cord.
SPLEEN: A large dark-red oval organ on the left side of the body between the stomach and the diaphragm.
STERNUM: The flat bone that articulates with the clavicles and the first seven pairs of ribs.
STEROID: Any of several fat-soluble organic compounds having as a basis 17 carbon atoms in four rings.
STOMACH: An enlarged and muscular saclike organ of the alimentary canal; the principal organ of digestion.
SYNAPSE: The junction between two neurons or between a neuron and a muscle.
SYSTOLE: The contraction of the chambers of the heart to drive blood into the aorta and pulmonary artery.
TAILBONE: The end of the vertebral column in humans and tailless apes.
TEETH: The hard white structures in the jaws used for biting and chewing.
TEMPLE: The flat area on either side of the forehead.
TENDON: A cord or band of inelastic tissue connecting a muscle with its bony attachment.
TESTICLE: One of the two male reproductive glands that produce spermatozoa and secrete androgens.
THALAMUS: Large egg-shaped structures of grey matter that form the dorsal subdivision of the diencephalon.
THIGH: The part of the leg between the hip and the knee.
THORACIC: Of or relating to the chest or thorax.
THORAX: The chest: the part of the body between the neck and the abdomen.
THROAT: The passage from the back of the mouth to the stomach and lungs.
THROMBOSIS: The formation or presence of a thrombus in a blood vessel.
THUMB: The thick short innermost digit of the forelimb.
THYMUS: A ductless glandular organ at the base of the neck.
THYROID: A gland in the neck that makes hormones controlling metabolism.
TIBIA: The inner and thicker of the two bones of the human leg between the knee and ankle.
TISSUE: Part of an organism consisting of an aggregate of cells having a similar structure and function.
TONGUE: A mobile mass of muscular tissue covered with mucous membrane and located in the oral cavity.
TONSIL: Either of two masses of lymphatic tissue one on each side of the oral pharynx.
TOOTH: One of the hard white structures in the jaws used for biting and chewing.
TORSO: The body excluding the head and neck and limbs.
TOXIN: A poison produced by a living organism.
TRACHEA: Membranous tube with cartilaginous rings that conveys inhaled air from the larynx to the bronchi.
TRACHEAL: Relating to or resembling or functioning like a trachea.
TRAPEZIUS: Either of two flat triangular muscles of the shoulder and upper back.
TRICEPS: The large muscle at the back of the upper arm.
TUMOR: An abnormal new mass of tissue that serves no purpose.
TUMOUR: An abnormal new mass of tissue that serves no purpose.
ULNA: The inner and longer of the two bones of the human forearm.
UMBILICAL: Of or relating to the navel or the umbilical cord.
UREA: The main nitrogen-containing waste in urine, made in the liver.
URETER: Either of a pair of thick-walled tubes that carry urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder.
URETHRA: Duct through which urine is discharged in most mammals and which serves as the male genital duct.
UTERUS: A hollow muscular organ in the pelvic cavity of females; contains the developing fetus.
UVULA: A small pendant fleshy lobe at the back of the soft palate.
VACCINE: A preparation that trains the immune system to fight a disease.
VASCULAR: Of or relating to or having vessels that conduct and circulate fluids.
VEIN: A blood vessel that carries blood from the capillaries toward the heart.
VENOUS: Of or contained in or performing the function of the veins.
VENTRICLE: Either of the two lower chambers of the heart, which pump blood out.
VERTEBRA: One of the bony segments of the spinal column.
VERTEBRAE: One of the bony segments of the spinal column.
VERTEBRAL: Of or relating to or constituting vertebrae.
VESICLE: A small anatomically normal sac or bladderlike structure.
VESSEL: A tube in which a body fluid circulates.
VILLUS: One of the tiny finger-like projections lining the small intestine.
VIRUS: A tiny infectious agent that can multiply only inside living cells.
VISCERAL: Relating to or affecting the viscera.
VITAMIN: Any of a group of organic substances essential in small quantities to normal metabolism.
VITREOUS: Of or relating to or constituting the vitreous humor of the eye.
WAIST: The narrowing of the body between the ribs and hips.
WINDPIPE: Membranous tube with cartilaginous rings that conveys inhaled air from the larynx to the bronchi.
WRINKLE: A crease or fold in the skin.
WRIST: A joint between the distal end of the radius and the proximal row of carpal bones.
ZYGOMATIC: The arch of bone beneath the eye that forms the prominence of the cheek.
